For flying, I'd recommend a USB-C power bank between 10,000 and 20,000mAh, ideally with 30W–65W charging.

The most important factors are airline compatibility, size, weight, and charging speed—not just battery capacity.

What makes a power bank good for flying?

10,000mAh: Best for short flights, lightweight, roughly 1–2 phone charges.

20,000mAh: Best overall for long flights and international travel, roughly 3–4 phone charges.

25,000–27,000mAh: Best for charging laptops or multiple devices, but heavier.

USB-C PD: Look for at least 30W for phones and 65W or more for many laptops.

Airline rule: Power banks belong in carry-on baggage, never checked baggage. In the US, batteries up to 100Wh are generally permitted, but airlines may impose additional restrictions on quantity and onboard use.

Important 2026 airline restrictions

The FAA permits power banks up to 100Wh in carry-on luggage, but the 2026 IATA guidance limits passengers to two power banks and advises against using them to charge devices onboard. Some airlines have adopted stricter rules, so check your carrier before departure.
